stories.title: Teen girl charged with murder over recording of San Diego mosque attack
stories.summary: A 17-year-old girl has been charged with murder by aiding and abetting after prosecutors say she recorded a livestream of an attack on a San Diego mosque that left three people dead. Prosecutors say the girl also published a manifesto from two teenage gunmen who carried out the attack on the Islamic Center of San Diego on 18 May. The teenager, from North Carolina, was arrested last week and indicted by a grand jury on Monday, according to Forsyth County District Attorney Jim O'Neill. Speaking at a news conference, O'Neill said: "The thought of her going back to school, with the weekend approaching, holy days approaching, we didn't know what she was capable of." The teenager now faces three murder charges and one count of conspiracy. O'Neill explained that under North Carolina law, a person accused of aiding and abetting a crime can be held criminally responsible in the same way as the person who carried it out. Authorities say the attack was carried out by two males - aged 17 and 18 - who opened fire at the mosque, before taking their own lives. O'Neill said the pair had two aims that day: "Number one, to kill as many people as possible on that day. Secondly, they wanted this carnage and destruction recorded... livestreamed." A security guard at the mosque, Amin Abdullah, exchanged gunfire with the attackers and initiated a lockdown, helping protect around 140 children who were inside the building. Abdullah and two worshippers - Mansour Kaziha and Nader Awad, who drew the attentions of the shooters in a parking lot - were fatally shot.

stories.title: Gas inventories in European storage facilities exceed 65%
stories.summary: This is the lowest level recorded for this date since data collection began in 2011
article_sentences: MOSCOW, September 1.

Gas inventories in Europe's underground storage facilities have exceeded 65%, but remain at their lowest level for this time of year since records began in 2011, according to TASS calculations based on data from Gas Infrastructure Europe (GIE).
As of August 30, European underground gas storage facilities were 65.09% full, 16.87 percentage points below the five-year average for that date, compared with 77.4% a year earlier.
This is the lowest level recorded for this date since data collection began in 2011.
EU storage facilities hold around 71.1 bln cubic meters of gas, 13.9 bln cubic meters less than a year earlier and the lowest volume since 2013.
Gazprom previously forecast that gas inventories in European underground storage facilities may not even reach 75% by the next heating season.
Net injections (the difference between the volume of gas injected into and withdrawn from storage) into EU underground storage facilities in August 2026 are also at their lowest level in six years.
Since the beginning of April, Europe has injected only 59% of the gas needed for the coming winter, or 40 bln cubic meters.
TASS previously reported that Europe risks entering the heating season with record-low gas inventories.

The average rate of replenishment at underground gas storage facilities in EU countries in July was among the lowest recorded since data collection began in 2011 and accelerated only slightly in August.

At these rates, Europe's storage facilities may be only 70-75% full by the traditional start of the fall-winter period, which would be the lowest level ever recorded at the beginning of a heating season.
Under European Commission requirements, EU countries must ensure that their gas storage facilities are 90% full between October 1 and December 1 each year.
